subdomain: 3.8 Evaluate progressive discovery vs. monolithic context strategy

en.question: An inspection assistant has four compact tools, and every supported task needs all four. Tool selection is accurate and definition tokens are negligible. A proposed progressive-discovery design would require a search before those same tools become available. Which starting configuration is best justified by these facts?

options.text: Load the four definitions directly and introduce discovery only if measured catalog growth or selection problems justify it.
options.note: Direct loading is simple when the compact toolset is always relevant. Discovery would add a step without avoiding meaningful unused definition context in this workload.

options.text: Require discovery for every tool because on-demand loading always reduces total completion latency.
options.note: Discovery adds a search step before invocation. When all definitions are small and always needed, there is no established latency benefit to offset that step.

options.text: Split the same four tools into vendor-specific deferred groups that are discovered separately.
options.note: All four tools are needed for every task, so grouping does not avoid loading irrelevant capabilities. Separate discovery steps add overhead to an already small and accurate configuration.

options.text: Replace the four tools with one autonomous dispatcher that selects and invokes them through another model turn.
options.note: Another model-selected dispatcher adds orchestration to an already accurate, compact toolset. No catalog or selection problem in the scenario calls for that additional layer.

references.title: Anthropic Engineering: Introducing advanced tool use
